courses.title: Application Support Fundamentals
courses.subtitle: What the job actually is
courses.description: Learn the role, the teams, the environments, and the tools behind a software company's support desk. The vocabulary and mental map you need before your first interview or shift.

courses.title: Troubleshooting and Debugging
courses.subtitle: A repeatable method that holds up in interviews
courses.description: A structured method for diagnosing application problems: capture the report, gather evidence, test one hypothesis at a time, and document what you learned so it never costs a day again.

courses.title: SQL for Application Support
courses.subtitle: Find the data behind the ticket
courses.description: Answer real support questions from a small support database: ticket statuses and priorities, joins to customers and agents, and counts that prove what is happening. Every query runs in the page.

courses.title: Tickets, Incidents and ITIL
courses.subtitle: How support work is tracked and prioritised
courses.description: How a SaaS support team records and runs real work: clear ticket fields, P1-P4 priorities and SLAs, the major-incident lifecycle, problem and change records, and escalation that never drops the customer.

courses.title: Linux and the Command Line for Support
courses.subtitle: Navigate, inspect, and grab evidence fast
courses.description: Nearly every SaaS server runs Linux. Learn the shell commands support engineers use every day to navigate a box, read its logs, check its resources, and prove what happened.

courses.title: Logs, Monitoring and Alerting
courses.subtitle: Know before the customer does
courses.description: Read a log line like a detective, turn noisy output into signal, and use metrics and alerts so your team hears about trouble before the customer does.

courses.title: Communication and Customer Service
courses.subtitle: Write so users trust you
courses.description: The writing, questioning and de-escalation skills that make support engineers effective: first replies people trust, questions that actually get answered, honest bad news, calm handling of angry users, and handoffs engineers can act on.

courses.title: Interviewing for Application Support
courses.subtitle: Turn your experience into an offer
courses.description: Prepare the parts of an Application Support interview that are actually rehearseable: reading the job ad, STAR stories, technical and behavioural scenarios, take-home ticket exercises, and the questions you ask back.

courses.title: Linux & the Command Line, In Depth
courses.subtitle: Weeks 1-2: navigate, inspect and shape a Linux box
courses.description: A deep, hands-on tour of the Linux shell for anyone heading into data or platform work: the filesystem, permissions, searching, pipes, text processing with sed/awk, and processes, services and cron.

courses.title: Bash Scripting & Automation
courses.subtitle: Week 3: turn commands into reliable scripts
courses.description: Write Bash scripts that automate real work: variables and quoting, arguments and exit codes, conditionals and loops, functions and arrays, safe scripting with set -euo pipefail and traps, and a full backup-script walkthrough.

courses.title: Git & Version Control
courses.subtitle: Weeks 3-4: track every change with confidence
courses.description: Version control from first principles: the working tree and staging area, commits and history, branching and merging, remotes and pull requests, safely rewriting history, and recovering from mistakes.

courses.title: SQL Fundamentals
courses.subtitle: Weeks 5-7: query any relational database
courses.description: Build SQL from the ground up on a realistic sample database: selecting and filtering rows, NULLs, sorting, aggregates, joining tables, subqueries, and an introduction to CTEs and window functions. Most lessons have runnable queries.

courses.title: PostgreSQL Essentials
courses.subtitle: Week 8: types, psql, indexes, EXPLAIN and transactions
courses.description: Go under the hood of PostgreSQL: rich data types and constraints, the psql CLI, how indexes actually work, reading EXPLAIN plans, and how transactions, MVCC and locking keep concurrent writes correct.

courses.title: SQL Performance Tuning
courses.subtitle: Week 9: make slow queries fast
courses.description: A practical method for speeding up slow queries: read the execution plan, design the right index, rewrite the query, keep statistics fresh, resolve lock contention, and use materialized views and partitioning on large tables.

courses.title: PostgreSQL Operations
courses.subtitle: Week 10: back up, replicate and secure a Postgres server
courses.description: The day-two operations that keep a database safe: backups and point-in-time recovery, replication and read replicas, roles and least-privilege access, connection pooling with pgbouncer, and the maintenance routine every DBA owns.

courses.title: Python for Data
courses.subtitle: Weeks 11-14: script, transform and load data
courses.description: From your first script to a working ETL job: Python basics and virtual environments, control flow and comprehensions, functions and error handling, files with pathlib/CSV/JSON, pandas dataframes, groupby and merges, and talking to a database with parameterized queries.

courses.title: AWS Cloud Foundations
courses.subtitle: Weeks 15-18: where data lives and runs
courses.description: Learn one cloud deeply and map the rest: accounts and the shared model, IAM and least privilege, S3 storage, EC2 and security groups, VPC networking, managed databases with RDS, serverless with Lambda, and infrastructure as code with Terraform.

courses.title: dbt Analytics Engineering
courses.subtitle: Weeks 19-22: tested, versioned SQL transformations
courses.description: Turn raw tables into a documented, tested warehouse with dbt: models and the DAG, sources and staging, materializations including incremental, tests as quality gates, docs and lineage, and macros with snapshots for slowly changing dimensions.

courses.title: Docker & Kubernetes Essentials
courses.subtitle: Weeks 23-25: package and run services anywhere
courses.description: Containerise applications and run them on a cluster: images vs containers, writing Dockerfiles, volumes and networking, Docker Compose for multi-service stacks, then Kubernetes pods, deployments, services, config, storage and Helm.

courses.title: Capstone & Interview Prep
courses.subtitle: Week 26: turn the work into an offer
courses.description: The finishing week: assemble a capstone project that proves you can do the job end to end, add tests and CI, drill the SQL and Linux interview scenarios, write STAR stories from your support experience, and rehearse the portfolio walkthrough that turns practice into an offer.
